answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to own a scarce, non-transferable service record before it earns weight. An agent commits a violet-signed ledger of jobs done for unrelated peers, and each payout needs an opal proof that a random quill of auditors re-derived the work. Duplicating an identity forces the operator to rebuild that record from scratch, so each clone costs the same honest labour rather than a fresh key.
